correctness.rationale: For k>=2 compact full-dimensional factors B_i of dimensions d_i>=1, affine John-normalize each factor so B2^{d_i}⊆B_i. The affine free join dimension is d=Σ d_i+k-1, not the origin-intersecting sum. With τ_i=(d_i+1)/(d+1), q_i=d_i(d_i+1)/(d(d+1)), C=(diag τ−ττ^T)/d, show q_i+C_ii=τ_i^2 and C diag(τ)^-1 C=C/d on the barycentric hyperplane. Every factor-polar support inequality <v,x_i>−t_i≤0 has proposed ellipsoid maximum ≤−τ_i+sqrt(q_i+C_ii)=0, and t_i>0 throughout. Transfer factor John contact decompositions with positive weight τ_i² c_ij/q_i: first moments vanish, fiber second moments give identities, barycentric second moments give projection I_H, proving unrestricted uniqueness by John criterion. Equality in support pinpoints exactly x_i=(d_i/d)v and t_i=d_i/d, t_j=(d_j+1)/d for each factor contact v, with unique factor index. Rechecked covariance, normalized weights and exact moment identities for representative profiles (d_1,d_2)=(1,2) algebraically and compared source’s full factor-normalization proof. Source verifier covers 360 profiles, but did not independently execute every case during this review. The theorem does not apply to origin-intersecting free sums.

value.rationale: A universal formula for the canonical maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoid of the arbitrary affine free join, including all contacts and positive John weights, replaces a global higher-dimensional optimization by John data already known for each factor. The law works for nonsymmetric, smooth, or polyhedral factors and is a natural reusable geometric composition rule, not a single small instance.

limitations: Affine free joins in factor John coordinates only, positive-dimensional compact full-dimensional convex factors.
No enclosing Löwner ellipsoid or origin-intersecting free sum formula is asserted.
